title: 3Sum
description: Given an integer array nums, return all the triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j, i != k, j != k, and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0. Notice that the solution set must not contain duplicate triplets.
hints: Sort the array first. Then for each element, use two pointers to find pairs that sum to its negative.

optimalSolution.approach: Sort array. For each index i, use two pointers l=i+1, r=n-1. Skip duplicates at each pointer. Adjust pointers based on sum comparison.

followUpQuestions: How do you handle duplicate triplets?
Can you do better than O(n^2)?
interviewerNotes: Combines sorting + two pointers + duplicate handling. Common failure points: forgetting to skip duplicates, off-by-one errors on pointer movement. Key test for medium-level candidates.
